lead: Aircraft parts are made by forming sheet, machining or extruding metal, or laying up composite. They are then joined by rivets, bolts, adhesive or welding. The joint, not the plate, usually decides the strength, because holes cut the net section and load must pass from one part to another. Only a few universities teach fabrication as a full topic. The ideas matter for every spar, rib, frame and skin panel.
prereq: You need Aerospace materials and their behaviour for material allowables and Typical wing and fuselage structures for which members are joined.

blocks.text: Sheet metal is formed by pressing or stretching it over a die. Stretch forming pulls a clamped sheet over a curved die; the skin stretches plastically and keeps the die shape. Machining cuts a spar or fitting from a solid billet when the shape is thick and few parts are needed. Extrusion pushes hot metal through a die to make long constant-section stringers. Composite parts are laid up ply by ply on a mould and cured in an autoclave under heat and pressure.

The route is: raw sheet or billet, form or machine, surface treatment, jig assembly, joining, inspection. Surface treatment means anodising aluminium or priming it before assembly; the bare metal corrodes and the adhesive needs a clean, prepared surface. A jig holds the parts in their true shape while holes are drilled and fasteners are placed. Inspection checks hole size, fastener grip (the total thickness a fastener clamps, which sets the fastener length) and the finished shape, and repairs are made before the part leaves the shop.

Rivets are the standard aircraft fastener. A rivet fills its hole, and the driven head clamps the sheets. Bolts carry larger loads and can be removed. Adhesive bonding spreads load over a wide area and avoids holes, but needs careful surface preparation. Seam welding joins thin sheets along a line.

Joints are lap or butt. In a lap joint the load path is eccentric: the sheets are offset, so the joint also feels bending. A butt joint with splice plates is more symmetric. A group of fasteners shares load; the outer rows usually take more, not equal share. Check three things: rivet shear, bearing of the rivet on the sheet, and net-section tension with the holes removed. Rivets are set at least about two diameters from a sheet edge, so the sheet does not tear out in front of the hole. Holes also start fatigue cracks; an interference-fit bolt squeezes the hole and slows crack growth. Sealant keeps moisture out.
P<sub>shear</sub> = n τ πd²/4    P<sub>bearing</sub> = n d t σ<sub>br</sub>    P<sub>net</sub> = (w − n d) t σ<sub>t</sub>
blocks.where: n is the number of rivets in the row; d is the rivet diameter in m; t is the thinner sheet thickness in m; w is the sheet width in m; τ, σ<sub>br</sub> and σ<sub>t</sub> are the allowable rivet shear, sheet bearing and sheet tensile stresses in Pa. The joint strength is the smallest of the three.

figure.caption: The joint of worked example 2: two 2 mm sheets, 60 mm wide, lapped and joined by three 5 mm rivets in one row. Rivet shear (10.6 kN) is weaker than bearing (15.0 kN) and the net section through the holes (27.0 kN), so it sets the strength, 29 % of the uncut sheet.

examples.question: A single lap joint uses 4 rivets of 4 mm diameter. The allowable shear stress of the rivet material is 200 MPa. Find the load the joint can carry in rivet shear if all four rivets share it equally.
steps: Rivet diameter d = 4 mm = 0.004 m. Area A = π d²/4 = π × 0.004² ÷ 4 = 1.257 × 10⁻⁵ m² (12.57 mm²).
Allowable shear stress τ = 200 MPa = 200 × 10⁶ N/m². Load per rivet F₁ = τ A = 200 × 10⁶ × 1.257 × 10⁻⁵ = 2513 N.
Four rivets share equally: total F = 4 × 2513 = 10 053 N.
examples.answer: In rivet shear the joint carries about 10 053 N, or 10.1 kN, with ideal equal sharing; bearing, net section and the eccentricity of a single lap must still be checked.

examples.question: Two 2024-T3 sheets, each 2 mm thick and 60 mm wide, are joined in a single lap by one row of 3 rivets of 5 mm diameter across the width. Allowables: rivet shear 180 MPa, sheet bearing 500 MPa, sheet net-section tension 300 MPa. Find the strength of the joint, the mode that governs, and the joint efficiency against the uncut sheet.
steps: Net section: three holes remove 3 × 5 = 15 mm of the 60 mm width, so the net width is 45 mm. P = 0.045 × 0.002 × 300 × 10⁶ = 27 000 N.
The smallest value governs: rivet shear, 10 603 N.
Uncut sheet strength = 0.060 × 0.002 × 300 × 10⁶ = 36 000 N. Efficiency = 10 603 ÷ 36 000 = 0.295, about 29 %.
examples.answer: The joint carries 10.6 kN and fails in rivet shear; bearing (15.0 kN) and net section (27.0 kN) are stronger. Its efficiency is about 29 %, so a second row of rivets or larger rivets would be needed to use the sheet well.

traps: Stopping at rivet shear. Check bearing and net section; they often govern.
Using gross sheet area instead of net area through the holes.
Forgetting eccentricity in a single lap joint, which adds bending.
Assuming all rivets in a group share load equally; outer rows carry more.
Using the thicker sheet in the bearing check. Bearing uses the thinner sheet, because it crushes first.

quiz.q: Name three joining methods for aircraft structures.
quiz.a: Riveting, bolting and adhesive bonding; welding is also used.

quiz.q: Why is a butt joint preferred over a single lap for fatigue?
quiz.a: A butt joint is symmetric, so it avoids the eccentric bending that a single lap joint puts on the fasteners and sheets.

quiz.q: Two 1.6 mm sheets 50 mm wide are joined by one row of 2 rivets of 4 mm diameter. Allowables: rivet shear 200 MPa, bearing 480 MPa, net tension 290 MPa. Find the joint strength and the mode that governs.
Why does a hole reduce fatigue life more than static strength?
quiz.a: The hole raises local stress and starts a crack; static strength falls only by the lost net area, but repeated load grows the crack.

quiz.q: What does an interference-fit bolt do to the hole?
quiz.a: It squeezes the hole, leaves compressive stress around it and slows fatigue crack growth.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a jig in assembly?
quiz.a: It holds parts in their true shape while holes are drilled and fasteners are placed.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, automated drilling and interference-fit bolting dominate wing assembly, while composites shift the joint to bonded and co-cured interfaces. Search terms: stretch forming, autoclave cure, net-section bearing, interference fit fatigue.
